message.content:
Here are some of the most popular books written by J.K. Rowling:

| Title | Year | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| **Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone** (also *Sorcerer’s Stone* in the U.S.) | 1997 | First book in the globally‑famous Harry Potter series. |
| **Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets** | 1998 | Second installment, continuing the adventures of Harry and friends. |
| **Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban** | 1999 | Introduces key characters like Sirius Black and the Marauder’s Map. |
| **Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire** | 2000 | Features the Triwizard Tournament and the return of Voldemort. |
| **Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix** | 2003 | Explores the rise of the Ministry’s opposition to the wizarding world. |
| **Harry Potter and the Half‑Blood Prince** | 2005 | Provides backstory on Voldemort’s rise and the final battle. |
| **Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows** | 2007 | Concludes the epic saga with the final showdown. |
| **The Casual Vacancy** | 2012 | Rowling’s first adult novel, a political drama set in a small English town. |
| **The Ickabog** | 2020 | A children’s fable released as a free online book during the COVID‑19 pandemic. |
| **Cormoran Strike Series** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2013–present | A detective mystery series featuring private investigator Cormoran Strike and his assistant Robin Ellacott. |
| **The Cuckoo’s Calling** (first in the Cormoran Strike series) | 2013 | The debut novel under the pseudonym Robert Galbraith. |
| **The Silkworm** | 2014 | Second book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **Career of Evil** | 2015 | Third book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **Lethal White** | 2018 | Fourth book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **The Midnight Library** | 2020 | A speculative fiction novel about choices and alternate lives (published under her own name). |

These titles represent the breadth of Rowling’s work—from the beloved wizarding world to adult fiction and crime thrillers—each of which has garnered significant readership and critical acclaim.
